social.hook: They opened with 'Being Boiled' and closed with 'Together in Electric Dreams' — 17 songs between two perfect bookends.
social.caption: My first Human League show, and The English Beat opened. I didn't see them again for 15 years.
beats: First time seeing The Human League — August 2003, with The English Beat opening the night.
'Being Boiled' to start. 'Together in Electric Dreams' to close. Seventeen songs in between.
2003 was that kind of year: Peter Gabriel, Joe Jackson, The Cure — and now this.
It would be 15 years before I saw them again. I had no idea that night was going to have to last that long.

social.hook: He opened with 'Steppin' Out' and closed with 'I'm the Man' — 20 songs in between.
social.caption: First time I saw Joe Jackson, and he played the whole room like he had something to prove. 'Steppin' Out' first, 'I'm the Man' last — nothing soft about that setlist.
beats: 23 years ago tonight, I saw Joe Jackson for the first time — House of Blues Anaheim, August 2003.
He opened with 'Steppin' Out'. Not buried mid-set, not saved for the encore. First song.
Twenty songs across the night, and he closed with 'I'm the Man' — which is a statement.
2003 was a good year for this. Peter Gabriel, The Human League, The Cure — and now this show in the count too.

social.hook: Third time seeing them, first and only time at this room.
social.caption: I've seen The Smithereens three times, and Birchmere was the last of them — still the only night I've spent in that room. Ten years today.
beats: August 26, 2016. The Smithereens at Birchmere — my first and only night in that room.
It was the third time I'd seen them. Some bands you keep finding reasons to go back for.
2016 also gave me Snarky Puppy and Prophets of Rage. The Smithereens fit that year in ways I didn't expect.
Ten years out, this one still sits at the end of the list. No fourth show yet.

social.hook: They closed with 'Love Will Tear Us Apart' — a Joy Division song, played by the band that survived it.
social.caption: New Order opened that night with 'State of the Nation' and closed with the song that defined what came before them. I didn't see them again for 37 years.
beats: August 23, 1985. A Certain Ratio and the Abecedarians opened. New Order headlined.
They opened with 'State of the Nation' — a song that felt like a statement about where they were going.
Fourteen songs later, they closed with 'Love Will Tear Us Apart.' Ian Curtis wrote it. They carried it.
I wouldn't see them again for 37 years. Some first shows take a long time to follow up.
